title: Looking for alpha users for PredixLab
author: wangqiao11
selftext: I'm one of the developers behind PredixLab, a US stock research tool for individual investors who like to make their own calls with data. unlike main other screener tools, we only focus on nasdaq-100 and S&P 500, and at the same, we provide pre-filtered signals, and it's easy to integrate with your own personal agent like grok bot, chatgpt, codex, etc.

comments.author: wangqiao11
comments.body:
What we're offering alpha users:

\- visit [https://predixlab.com](https://predixlab.com/) for registration.

\- After you sign up, email [contact@predixlab.com](mailto:contact@predixlab.com) from your account's email address and we'll add one more month of Premium. No payment method needed.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: an agent handed a bare 'bullish on X' can't tell a fresh signal from a week-old one, so I'd send the date and the numbers behind each signal along with it. there's a cheap way to check a feed like yours too: I built Quantradin, where people connect their own AI and it trades US stocks with pretend money, so the signals could be scored there before anyone leans on them. quantradin.com. what does a signal look like when it reaches the agent?

replies.author: wangqiao11
replies.body: Predixlab provides various of information, alpha ranks, possible tops/bottoms, abnormal options, user need to build their own strategies if they want the agent to automatically trade stocks based on the information. So basically, I just provide pre-filtered market data to agents that what it should take care of today. Agents can do deep analysis for given stocks instead of monitoring entire markets, which should be more efficient and less cost.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: makes sense, deep work on ten names beats shallow watching of five thousand. as a user I'd check the filter itself then: of the stocks that made your possible-bottom list last month, how many went on to bottom. publish that count and alpha users have a reason to trust the shortlist.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the number I'd swap out is max return. nobody sells at the best price of the next 20 days, so it flatters every signal, and a random pick would show a decent max too. the close on day 20 next to the worst dip along the way would tell a user what they'd really have sat through.

replies.author: wangqiao11
replies.body: It just shows the signal performance, not a promise of returns in reality.
